title: Optimization of TiO2/SiO2 Bilayer with Analytical Quarter-Wave Initialization
scientific_hypothesis: Swapping the layer order to TiO2 (high index) adjacent to air and SiO2 (low index) adjacent to glass, combined with an initialization based on the analytical quarter-wave condition at the spectral center (575 nm), will allow the gradient optimizer to converge to a distinct local minimum with a lower broadband mean reflectance than the SiO2-first configuration found in Round 1.
design_principle: Impedance matching via a high-to-low index transition (Air->TiO2->SiO2->Glass) often provides a smoother effective index gradient than low-to-high for this specific substrate/incident pair. Initializing near the theoretical single-wavelength optimum ($d = \λ_c / 4n$) reduces the risk of the optimizer settling in a shallow local minimum far from the physical resonance condition.
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm
achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference
manufacturing_considerations: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm
exactly one layer of TiO2 and one layer of SiO2
theory_basis: Quarter-wave antireflection condition: $n_1 d_1 = n_2 d_2 = \λ_c/4$ for zero reflectance at a single wavelength.
Effective medium theory suggesting high-index-first ordering may better match the large Air-Glass index jump.
expected_advantages: Potential to escape the local minimum found in the SiO2-first topology.
Analytical initialization provides a physically grounded starting point closer to the global optimum.
known_risks: The TiO2-first order might yield a higher minimum reflectance due to stronger Fresnel reflections at the first interface if not perfectly tuned.
The quarter-wave thicknesses for 575 nm might fall outside the 40-160 nm bounds or require scaling that distorts the broadband response.
execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic TMM optimization for a planar stack: Incident Medium (Air, n=1.0) | Layer 1 (TiO2, n=2.40, lossless) | Layer 2 (SiO2, n=1.46, lossless) | Substrate (Glass, n=1.52, lossless). Constraints: Both layer thicknesses must be between 40 nm and 160 nm. Objective: Minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450 nm to 700 nm (5 nm steps). Optimization Settings: Use seed 17, maximum 64 solver evaluations. Initialize the optimizer with the analytical quarter-wave thicknesses for the center wavelength 575 nm: initial_thickness_TiO2 = 575/(4*2.40) nm, initial_thickness_SiO2 = 575/(4*1.46) nm. If these initial values fall outside the [40, 160] nm bounds, clamp them to the nearest bound before starting the optimization run. Report the final optimized thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.
revision_reason: Feedback directive requested swapping the layer order (TiO2 first) and using an analytical quarter-wave initialization at 575 nm to explore a different region of the design space compared to Round 1's SiO2-first random/gradient start.
